extracted.intended_audience: Authors submitting to Nature Portfolio journals, institutional press officers, and journalists covering Nature content
extracted.subtask_description: Policies and guidance governing authors' and journalists' interactions with the media around submissions and accepted papers for Nature Portfolio journals, including embargo rules, preprint and conference presentation treatment, and press-release procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Soliciting media coverage of submitted material
rubrics_metrics.description: We strongly discourage authors and potential authors from direct solicitation of media coverage of material they have submitted to Nature and the Nature Portfolio journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accepted contributions can be discussed with the media only once the publication date has been confirmed and no more than a week before the publication date under our embargo conditions. The page also notes the journal 'strongly discourage[s] the direct soliciting of media coverage to appear ahead of publication of the final version of a paper.' (Anti-pattern: contacting journalists to publicize a manuscript before acceptance/confirmed publication.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Embargoed distribution of press releases and early access to papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Nature produces and distributes press releases summarizing upcoming content to a list of registered journalists; journalists receive access to the full text of papers about a week before publication on a password-protected website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists are encouraged to read the full paper and are given names and contact details of corresponding authors. The content of the press release and papers is embargoed until the time and date clearly stated on the press release. (Practical note: access is password-protected and timed to be about a week before publication.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial selection and highlighting of newsworthy papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers deemed especially newsworthy are highlighted by a brief summary on the press release for that journal, written by the editors and the press office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may receive calls or emails from the media during this time; they are encouraged to cooperate so coverage is accurate and balanced. (Implication: editors decide which papers receive special highlighting; authors should expect greater media attention and be prepared to engage responsibly.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Authors arranging their own publicity must adhere to embargoes
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors whose papers are scheduled for publication may arrange their own publicity (for instance through their institutional press offices), but they must strictly adhere to our media embargo and are advised to coordinate their own publicity with our press office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordination with the journal press office is advised to avoid breaking embargoes or pre-empting journal communications. (Anti-pattern: independent publicity that violates the embargo.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and rationale for embargoes
rubrics_metrics.description: The Nature Portfolio journals' policy is to release information in a way that provides fair and equal access to the media, allowing informed comment based on the complete and final version of the paper to be published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embargoes are intended to serve scientists, authors, journalists and the public by enabling informed comment and allowing institutional press offices and authors to interact with the media ahead of publication. The page emphasizes that the benefits of peer review give journalists confidence in new work and that premature release removes journalists' ability to obtain independent reactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harm of premature release and need for confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Premature release to the media denies journalists the confidence provided by peer review and removes the ability to obtain informed reactions from independent researchers in the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are expected to keep details of the peer review and editorial process confidential. (Anti-pattern: publicly revealing peer-review details or releasing results to media before the embargoed publication date.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions for breaking embargoes
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists who break our embargoes have been removed from the press-release circulation list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The journal will continue to use this sanction when appropriate. (Implication: repeated or serious breaches risk loss of privileged prepublication access.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of preprints and conference presentations
rubrics_metrics.description: Nature Portfolio journals support open communications such as posting on recognised preprint servers or discussing at research meetings; neither conference presentations nor posting on recognized preprint servers constitute prior publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Researchers may display drafts on established preprint servers before or during submission; exposure of preprints does not preempt submission. The page references further policy details and editorials on preprints and encourages their use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance for engaging media about preprints or conference presentations
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers may respond to media requests in response to a preprint or conference presentation by providing explanation or clarification of the work or information about its context; such media coverage will not hinder editorial handling of the submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When speaking to reporters about preprints, researchers should make it clear the paper has not yet undergone peer review, that the findings are provisional and that the conclusions may change. The page also recommends that reporters who cover preprints clearly indicate that the study has not been peer reviewed. (Anti-pattern: allowing reporters to present preprint findings as final without noting provisional status.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for open researcher communication channels
rubrics_metrics.description: Nature Portfolio journals support open communications between researchers via community preprint servers, preprint commenting platforms, discussions at meetings or online collaborative sites such as wikis or the author's blog.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The policy stresses that they do not wish to hinder such communication and provides links to more information about preprint policies. (Practical implication: authors can use recognized open channels but should remain mindful of embargo and disclosure guidance when interacting with media.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact point for clarification
rubrics_metrics.description: If further clarification is required about press/embargo policy, contact the Nature Portfolio press office by e-mail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The press office is the advised liaison for coordination and questions regarding embargoes, publicity, and press-release matters.
